blurb: `Wire(…)` hands raw text to the real boundary, before any decoding, so that a case can check what the boundary refuses. Only a `system` case has a real boundary: below it the handler is called directly, and the text would go in unchecked. Promote the case with `as system`, or pass a typed value instead. For other addresses, see `bynk.test.wire_http_only`.
summary: A `Wire(...)` raw argument is used outside a `system`-tier service address; `Wire` hands pre-validation input to the boundary and is meaningless at `unit` or in any other position.
